intent:
CI cannot reach the cluster today. Every lab name resolves publicly to
`192.168.2.30`, a private address, so it works only on the LAN or through the
subnet route firebat advertises to the tailnet (`docs/reference/edge-routes.md`,
`.okf/components/tailscale-subnet-router.md`). The only workflows are
GitHub-hosted (`.github/workflows/ci.yaml`, `.github/workflows/claude-ollama.yaml`,
`.github/workflows/hermes-interactive.yaml`). Vault (`vault.lab.orangecluster.nl`)
and the OpenViking API (`openviking-api.lab.orangecluster.nl`) both sit behind
HAProxy on `192.168.2.30:443`, so CI needs that one destination. This ticket
builds the network path. `ci-openviking-sync` builds the Vault login and the
OpenViking sync on top of it.

Chosen approach: a GitHub-hosted runner joins the tailnet with the official
`tailscale/github-action` as an ephemeral node tagged `tag:ci`. Rejected: a
self-hosted runner on the cluster. The repository is public, and GitHub warns
against self-hosted runners on public repos because a fork's pull request can
run code on them. That would put a code executor on the LAN with no tailnet
policy in front of it. Also rejected: a Tailscale auth key as a repository
secret, because `.github/workflows/claude-ollama.yaml` is an agent with tool
use triggered by issue and PR text, and repository secrets are readable by
every workflow.

What changes where:

- **Tailnet policy, in the Tailscale admin console, where it lives today.**
  The repository has no ACL file. Add `tagOwners` for `tag:ci` and one grant
  from `tag:ci` to `192.168.2.30:443` and nothing else. Create a Tailscale
  credential that can only mint ephemeral, pre-approved `tag:ci` nodes:
  workload identity federation bound to this repository if the tailnet
  offers it, otherwise an OAuth client held in a GitHub Environment with a
  branch protection rule. The policy is the only network control. On
  firebat, tailscaled's `ts-input` chain accepts all `tailscale0` traffic
  ahead of ufw, and ufw forwards routed traffic unfiltered
  (`.okf/components/host-firewall.md`). The runner must accept subnet routes,
  which `tailscale up` on Linux does not do by default, so the action passes
  `--accept-routes`.
- **Workflow, `new:.github/workflows/tailnet-check.yaml`**: `workflow_dispatch`
  only, never `pull_request` or `pull_request_target`. It uses explicit
  `permissions`, the GitHub Environment and a timeout. It joins the tailnet,
  asserts the edge answers, and asserts the ports outside the grant time out.
  It stays as a manual diagnostic, and `ci-openviking-sync` reuses its join
  step.
- **Knowledge**: update `.okf/components/tailscale-subnet-router.md` with the
  `tag:ci` grant and a read-only copy of the policy stanza (the console stays
  authoritative). Add a decision record (`kmctl new decision`) for the runner
  choice and the Tailscale credential.

An earlier plan for this half, C1, is in git at `48f52e2`
(`.loop/plans/C1-cicd-tailscale-github-actions-deploy.md` there). Its points
on GitHub Environments, `workflow_dispatch` and `tagOwners` carry over. Its
dial target (HAProxy stats on firebat's tailnet address, port 8404) does not:
the sync needs the lab names, which need the subnet route.

Outcome: a `workflow_dispatch` run of `tailnet-check` on `main` joins the
tailnet as an ephemeral `tag:ci` node, which is gone from the console after
the run. From the runner, `https://vault.lab.orangecluster.nl/v1/sys/health`
and `https://openviking-api.lab.orangecluster.nl/health` answer over the
trusted certificate. `192.168.2.30:8200`, `192.168.2.50:1933` and firebat's
tailnet address on port 8200 time out. No Tailscale credential is in a
committed file or a repository-level secret. `just pre_commit` and
`uv run --directory cli pytest` pass.

# ci-tailscale-access

Relayed from: none

## Intent

`.github/workflows/hermes-interactive.yaml`). Vault (`vault.lab.orangecluster.nl`)
and the OpenViking API (`openviking-api.lab.orangecluster.nl`) both sit behind
HAProxy on `192.168.2.30:443`, so CI needs that one destination. This ticket
builds the network path. `ci-openviking-sync` builds the Vault login and the
OpenViking sync on top of it.

Chosen approach: a GitHub-hosted runner joins the tailnet with the official
`tailscale/github-action` as an ephemeral node tagged `tag:ci`. Rejected: a
self-hosted runner on the cluster. The repository is public, and GitHub warns
against self-hosted runners on public repos because a fork's pull request can

use triggered by issue and PR text, and repository secrets are readable by

  The repository has no ACL file. Add `tagOwners` for `tag:ci` and one grant
  from `tag:ci` to `192.168.2.30:443` and nothing else. Create a Tailscale
  credential that can only mint ephemeral, pre-approved `tag:ci` nodes:
  workload identity federation bound to this repository if the tailnet
  offers it, otherwise an OAuth client held in a GitHub Environment with a
  branch protection rule. The policy is the only network control. On
  firebat, tailscaled's `ts-input` chain accepts all `tailscale0` traffic
  ahead of ufw, and ufw forwards routed traffic unfiltered

- **Workflow, `new:.github/workflows/tailnet-check.yaml`**: `workflow_dispatch`

An earlier plan for this half, C1, is in git at `48f52e2`
(`.loop/plans/C1-cicd-tailscale-github-actions-deploy.md` there). Its points
on GitHub Environments, `workflow_dispatch` and `tagOwners` carry over. Its
dial target (HAProxy stats on firebat's tailnet address, port 8404) does not:
the sync needs the lab names, which need the subnet route.

Outcome: a `workflow_dispatch` run of `tailnet-check` on `main` joins the
tailnet as an ephemeral `tag:ci` node, which is gone from the console after
the run. From the runner, `https://vault.lab.orangecluster.nl/v1/sys/health`
and `https://openviking-api.lab.orangecluster.nl/health` answer over the
trusted certificate. `192.168.2.30:8200`, `192.168.2.50:1933` and firebat's
tailnet address on port 8200 time out. No Tailscale credential is in a
committed file or a repository-level secret. `just pre_commit` and
`uv run --directory cli pytest` pass.

## Could invalidate this plan

- Tailnet policy scope. Tailscale's default policy allows every source to
  reach every destination, and tagged nodes match `*`. If the live policy
  still carries such a rule, a `tag:ci` grant adds nothing and the runner
  reaches every tailnet device and the whole LAN through the subnet route,
  every port on firebat included. Fixing that rewrites access for every
  device on the tailnet, which is a scope change the operator must own, not a
  line added for CI. Spike question: does the live tailnet policy let a node
  tagged `tag:ci` reach anything besides `192.168.2.30:443`? With a grant to
  only that destination, does an ephemeral `tag:ci` node reach
  `https://vault.lab.orangecluster.nl` through the subnet route and time out
  on `192.168.2.30:8200` and firebat's tailnet address?
